root_cause.text: The `hci_le_create_big_complete_evt()` function lacks bounds checking on the loop counter `i` before accessing the flexible array `ev->bis_handle[i]`, allowing out-of-bounds reads when the controller reports fewer BIS handles than the number of pending BT_BOUND connections.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an explicit check `if (ev->num_bis <= i)` before accessing `ev->bis_handle[i++]`, which was missing in the original code. The CVE description confirms that "there is no check that i stays within ev->num_bis before the array access," and when this condition occurs, the loop reads "beyond the valid bis_handle[] flex array into adjacent heap memory," causing out-of-bounds values to be processed and creating an infinite loop when those invalid handles are rejected by `hci_conn_set_handle()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checking and error handling for BIS handle assignment in BIG creation to prevent out-of-bounds access and ensure proper connection cleanup on handle setup failures.
intent_record.what: Added two new guard clauses to the hci_le_create_big_complete_evt function: (1) a bounds check verifying ev->num_bis > i before accessing ev->bis_handle[i], and (2) error handling wrapping the hci_conn_set_handle call to catch and handle failures. Both clauses log errors, set ev->status to HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED, call hci_connect_cfm and hci_conn_del, then continue to the next iteration.
intent_record.how: The first guard prevents out-of-bounds array access by validating the BIS handle array index before dereferencing it. The second guard converts a silent failure mode (where hci_conn_set_handle errors were ignored) into explicit error handling that terminates the connection and notifies the caller. Together, these changes ensure the BIG (Broadcast Isochronous Group) is properly terminated when BIS (Broadcast Isochronous Stream) handles cannot be properly established.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add handling for HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED status to properly terminate BIG connections when an unexpected error occurs during creation.
intent_record.what: Modified the conditional check from `!ev->status && !i` to `ev->status == HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED || (!ev->status && !i)`, and added a multi-line comment explaining the termination logic for BIG (Broadcast Isochronous Group) connections.
intent_record.how: The change expands the condition that triggers BIG termination to include cases where an HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED status is returned, in addition to the existing case where status is success (0) but no BISes were connected. This ensures the BIG is terminated not only when no connections succeed, but also when an unspecified error occurs, preventing orphaned BIG resources.

This prevents out-of-bounds reads when the controller reports fewer BIS handles than expected, which is exactly the vulnerability described.

The group adds error handling for HCI_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED status to terminate BIG connections, which addresses error management but does not add bounds checking on the loop counter `i` before accessing `ev->bis_handle[i]`. The vulnerability root cause requires validation that `i` does not exceed the number of available BIS handles in the flexible array, which this change does not implement.

Direct array access to ev->bis_handle[i++] without prior validation that i is within bounds of the flexible array, enabling out-of-bounds memory access when the loop counter exceeds the number of available BIS handles.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function iterates through all connections in the hash list (line 6984) and increments counter `i` for each matching ISO_LINK connection (line 6991). However, there is no bounds checking to ensure that `i` does not exceed `ev->num_bis` before accessing `ev->bis_handle[i]` at line 6991. If the controller reports fewer BIS handles than the number of pending BT_BOUND connections, the array access `ev->bis_handle[i++]` will read beyond the allocated flexible array bounds. The vulnerability exists because the loop continues as long as there are matching connections in the list, but the array `bis_handle` is only guaranteed to have `ev->num_bis` elements (as validated in line 6977). There is no check like `if (i >= ev->num_bis) break;` before the array access.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct IS PRESENT in this commit. The code iterates through connections with `list_for_each_entry_rcu(conn, &hdev->conn_hash.list, list)` and accesses `ev->bis_handle[bis_idx++]` at line `conn->handle = __le16_to_cpu(ev->bis_handle[bis_idx++]);` without any bounds checking on `bis_idx` against `ev->num_bis`. The vulnerability exists because: (1) `bis_idx` is incremented for each matching connection found in the loop, (2) there is no check that `bis_idx < ev->num_bis` before accessing the flexible array `ev->bis_handle[bis_idx]`, and (3) if the controller reports fewer BIS handles than the number of pending connections bound to the BIG, an out-of-bounds read will occur. The code only checks `if (ev->num_bis)` in the old code path (removed in this commit) but provides no bounds validation in the new loop-based implementation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `hci_le_big_sync_established_evt()` (lines 6901-6945) contains the vulnerable construct. At line 6924, there is a loop `for (i = 0; i < ev->num_bis; i++)` that accesses `ev->bis[i]` without bounds checking. The vulnerability occurs because the loop counter `i` is only checked against `ev->num_bis` (which comes from the controller), but there is no validation that the actual flexible array `ev->bis` contains at least `ev->num_bis` elements. If a malicious or malfunctioning controller reports `ev->num_bis` greater than the actual number of BIS handles in the event, the loop will read out-of-bounds memory at line 6925: `u16 handle = le16_to_cpu(ev->bis[i]);`. The code does call `hci_le_ev_skb_pull()` at line 6918 to validate the skb length, but this validation is based on `flex_array_size(ev, bis, ev->num_bis)` - it trusts the `ev->num_bis` value from the controller without independent verification. There is no fix present in this commit to prevent accessing beyond the actual array bounds.
